summary: Building 3-D shapes from nets is a procedural skill that consolidates the 2-D to 3-D relationship. Children construct a net (measure, draw, cut, fold, tape), predict which solid it makes, then fold to verify and check that every face, edge and vertex of the built solid matches the target. Anchoring on a base face and adding faces as composites (e.g. a band of rectangles plus two triangular ends) reduces trial-and-error, and diagnosing why a faulty net won't close — gaps or overlaps — turns errors into structural learning. The worked example throughout is the triangular prism: two congruent triangles plus three rectangles, with 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices.
misconceptions: Falls back on the familiar cube 'cross' net and cannot generate a net for a different solid.
Chooses the wrong face-set (e.g. all rectangles, or two triangles and two rectangles for a prism).
Arranges the correct faces so the net cannot close; blames ragged cutting rather than the layout.

activities.title: Construct and fold the net of a triangular prism
steps: Using card, a ruler and scissors, draw the net of a triangular prism: two congruent triangles and three rectangles of equal length, each rectangle as wide as the triangle side it joins.
Before cutting, predict and say which shape will be the bottom (base) and which two shapes will cap the ends.
Cut out the net, fold along the edges and tape it shut.
Point to the finished solid and count its faces, edges and vertices (target: 5 faces, 9 edges, 6 vertices).
activities.insight: A valid net is more than the right set of faces — the faces must be arranged so they fold into a closed solid, and the structure of that solid (faces, edges, vertices) can be read off the built 3-D shape rather than the flat drawing.

activities.title: Drag-to-build a net and predict the fold
steps: Drag two triangles and three rectangles onto a grid to lay out a candidate net.
State which solid you predict it will make and which faces will be the base and the ends.
Fold the layout and watch how the rectangles and triangles move. Check whether every face meets its neighbour so the ends are capped and the prism closes.

If a face is left flapping or a gap or overlap appears, rearrange the faces so they meet correctly, for example by re-anchoring on a band of three rectangles with a triangle on each end, then fold again.
Rotate the sealed solid and tap round it to tally faces, edges and vertices.
activities.insight: A layout that 'looks fine' flat may still fail to close. Checking how each face will meet its neighbours when folded is what shows whether the prism seals. A band of three rectangles with triangular ends is one dependable layout, but not the only valid one.

activities.title: Compare and diagnose nets for the same solid
steps: Given several candidate nets for a triangular prism, sort them into those that will fold shut and those that will not.

For each failing net, say whether the problem is the face-set (wrong shapes, wrong number or mismatched sizes) or the arrangement (correct faces placed so that, when folded, some overlap or leave a gap).
Find two different valid nets for the same prism and explain why both work.
Reason about a near-miss: if a net has three triangles and two rectangles, could it fold into this prism, or into any closed solid at all? Explain using the faces a triangular prism needs.
activities.insight: Nets fail for two distinct reasons — the wrong set of faces, or a correct set arranged so it cannot close — and the same solid can have more than one valid net.

checkQuestion: Here is card, a ruler, and scissors. Construct the net of a triangular prism, then fold and tape it to check it makes the solid. When it is built, tell me how many faces, edges and vertices it has by pointing to them.
checkAnswer: Draws a net of two congruent triangles and three rectangles positioned so the rectangles form a band that wraps between the triangular ends; folds it to a closed prism with no gaps or overlaps; and, pointing to the built solid, counts 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices — self-correcting the layout if a first attempt won't close.
